sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Time first, from the job you have
sections.para: A startup needs time before money. Treat it as art, with money as a side effect. Start from your own revenue stream, start while employed, ask for part time, and treat savings, an exit or debt as buying time. Take investment later, and avoid regret.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Find time, buy time, and do not regret it
sections.para: Time is the resource. Improve the revenue you already have, cut streaming, start in a job, negotiate part time, and accept debt as a way to buy time, as Dinis did. There has never been a better time.

sections.label: Time first
sections.line: A startup is all-consuming, like art
sections.para: Funding depends on circumstances, but the main need is time. A founder is a creator who loves the work; money should follow success, not drive it, so the question is how to find time while earning a living.

sections.label: Start with your own revenue stream
sections.line: Make your existing revenue stream better first
sections.para: The best start is using the technology to improve work you already do, or selling to people you know. Even if that is all you achieve, it is a success; solving no real problem means chasing shadows.

sections.label: You have more time than you think
sections.line: Most people have more time than they think
sections.para: Anyone thinking of a startup usually has some success or few expenses and a drive to create. There is always time, starting with the hours that go to streaming.

sections.label: The best place to start is in a job
sections.line: The constraint of a job helps you focus
sections.para: Starting while employed gives income and therefore time, and limited hours force focus and shipping. Do it openly, with managers aware, on separate machines, never competing.

sections.label: Ask for part time
sections.line: Ask to go part time, as Dinis did
sections.para: Many employers prefer half of a good person to none. Dinis asked to go part time to build things elsewhere, offering a solution, and it worked; if you are not valued, leave anyway.

sections.label: It is a gamble
sections.line: Debt and an exit, used to buy time
sections.para: It is a gamble. Dinis cleared his debt, then went back into it for his GenAI startup, and uses exit money to pay himself instead of taking an executive role. Investment comes later, when profitable.

sections.label: Avoid regret
sections.line: Avoid regret; the pool is wider now
sections.para: There has never been a better time to create a company, but more people can, so competition is real. The expert in the problem has the advantage.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.para: Debt and an exit are personal. Part time depends on role and employer. Debt buys time only if you can carry it.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: A memo, and the related articles
sections.para: Dinis's memo of 19 October 2026, with the newsroom's articles on open source, selling, starting a company and funding.
